patch.objective: Identity and access management: user accounts, MFA, and permissions

sources.cite: CompTIA Server+ SK0-005 (V5) Exam Objectives, document version 7.0: Hardware 18%, Server Administration 30%, Security and Disaster Recovery 24%, Troubleshooting 28%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of CompTIA's PDF. Relevant text: 'Given a scenario, configure servers to use network infrastructure services' (name resolution, DNS); 'Explain the key concepts of high availability for servers' (load balancing); 'Given a scenario, configure and maintain server functions and features' (monitoring, performance: CPU); 'Given a scenario, troubleshoot common OS and software problems' (service failures; services and processes); 'Explain the importance of backups and restores' (backup validation); 'Explain important concepts pertaining to identity and access management for server administration' (user groups; permissions). The objective wording here is the course seed's.

sources.cite: inode(7), file mode bits: set-group-ID and sticky bit (man7.org, man-pages 6.19)
sources.note: Relevant text: 'For newly created files, the file group ID is either the group ID of the parent directory or the effective group ID of the creating process, depending on whether or not the set-group-ID bit is set on the parent directory'; 'The sticky bit (S_ISVTX) on a directory means that a file in that directory can be renamed or deleted only by the owner of the file, by the owner of the directory, and by a privileged process.' Read in full 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: -G, --groups: 'If the user is currently a member of a group which is not listed, the user will be removed from the group. This behaviour can be changed via the -a option, which appends the user to the current supplementary group list.' Read in full 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: ps format specifier supgrp, 'group names of supplementary groups, if any'; newgrp(1): 'The newgrp command is used to change the current group ID during a login session.' A running process keeps the supplementary groups it started with, so a group added with usermod reaches a user at the next login (the standard credentials model; credentials(7) read 2026-11-14). Read in full 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: octal modes, the setgid and sticky bits, and 'For directories chmod preserves set-user-ID and set-group-ID bits unless you explicitly specify otherwise.' Read in full 2026-11-14. Command output layouts are authored in each tool's style.
